key_insight: A coupled CEL simulation and ANN models can accurately predict friction stir welding quality in HDPE, showing that bottom preheating stabilizes heat and force while reducing defects.
engineering_relevance: The study provides actionable process windows for robust thermoplastic joining, especially for selecting rotation speed, traverse speed, and preheating to avoid wormholes and improve weld integrity.
method: 3D Coupled Eulerian-Lagrangian (CEL) model of HDPE FSW
Two multilayer perceptron ANNs trained on experimental temperature and axial-force data
Process-map comparison across rotation speed, welding speed, and bottom-surface preheating
evidence_signal: The ANN models achieved strong predictive performance with R2 values between 0.91 and 0.99, and the CEL model matched experimental void, thermal, and mechanical responses well.
watch_item: The optimized process window is based on the tested parameter range, so performance may change outside the studied speeds, preheating conditions, or material setup.
paper_title: Computational and machine learning modelling approaches for weld quality predictions in friction stir welding of high-density polyethylene
